title: VSEPR geometry, bond angles, and molecular polarity
objective: Predict domain and molecular geometry, assess angle changes, and determine whether bond dipoles cancel.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Count multiple bonds once. Keep “trigonal planar” and “trigonal pyramidal” distinct. Check terminal atom identities before claiming cancellation. Use the lone-pair positions for five and six domains.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: The prompt may ask separately for electron geometry, molecular geometry, ideal angle, or polarity. Name each from the corresponding step.

blocks.title: VSEPR and molecular geometry
blocks.focus: Pause and write AXE notation for each example before naming its shape.

blocks.title: Different shapes with four domains
blocks.answer: Both have tetrahedral electron geometry. Ammonia is trigonal pyramidal and water is bent. Both are polar.

steps.title: Count
steps.md: NH₃ is AX₃E and H₂O is AX₂E₂.
steps.why: Four domains determine the parent arrangement.

steps.title: Ignore lone pairs for the shape name
steps.md: Three bonded neighbors form a pyramid and two form a bend.

steps.title: Combine vectors
steps.md: For each molecule, the bond dipoles do not cancel.
steps.why: The hydrogens are arranged asymmetrically around the central atom.

blocks.title: Five and six domains
blocks.problem: Predict shape and polarity for $\ce{SF4}$ and $\ce{XeF4}$.
blocks.answer: SF₄ is seesaw and polar. XeF₄ is square planar and nonpolar.

steps.title: SF₄
steps.md: Four bonds and one equatorial lone pair give AX₄E.
steps.why: Five domains arrange first as trigonal bipyramidal.

steps.title: XeF₄
steps.md: Four bonds and two opposite lone pairs give AX₄E₂.
steps.why: The parent octahedral geometry leaves a square of attached F atoms.

steps.title: Polarity
steps.md: SF₄ dipoles do not cancel; XeF₄ has cancelling opposite F pairs.
steps.why: The net dipole depends on the occupied bond directions.
